- https://securinghardware.com/ (homepage, fetched) — mission statement re: applied physical attacks training; "Big Hack" caught off guard quote.

- https://securinghardware.com/articles/congrats-youre-rejected/ (fetched, PRIMARY) — 2018-06-04; CFP rejection reflection, 2nd-person advice on persistence/feedback, mentor framing.

## Extracted growth signals (first-person)
1. Career origin: CPU pre/post-silicon penetration testing → realized training leverage → founded SecuringHardware.com (~2012, per 2017 wrap-up "5th year").
2. Motivation: perceived industry gap ("dearth of information on hardware security practices").
3. Business approach: word-of-mouth growth, explicit rejection of "typical business status quo".
4. Failure/feedback handling: CFP rejection article frames persistence + seeking feedback as the response to decline; functions as mentor-playbook.
5. Tool building: Tigard, Erebus (open-source hw).
6. Community anchoring: BSides Portland, CTRL-H Hackerspace, ToorCamp — self-described "superpower" for conversation.
7. Early teaching roots: DEFCON 21 (2013) timing side-channel workshops in HW Hacking Village; BSides PDX/Seattle 2013.

## Gaps
- No retrieved long-form external podcast/AMA/long-interview transcript (Risky Business etc.) — searches returned summaries, not fetchable episode URLs.
- Education, specific prior employers beyond CPU-pentest role, named mentors: not present in fetched material.
- Exact dates (founding year) inferred as ~2012 from 2017-wrapup "5th successful year" — inferred not documented as explicit date.
- 2018-06-04 rejection article is advisory (2nd person); no personal anecdote of a specific rejection of his own disclosed.

## Status
Evidence complete enough for documented (first-person primary) on career-origin/founding + reported on community/tool building. Output drafted.
